structure.title: Establishing the experiment
structure.text: Opening chapters account for shelter, expenses, and the decision to live by the pond. Practical detail supports the philosophical claims.

structure.title: A year of attention
structure.text: The arrangement moves through work, visitors, animals, weather, and seasons, turning repeated observation into reflection.

context.title: A shaped experiment
context.text: The book arranges experience into a seasonal pattern. It is neither a complete diary nor a claim to have escaped every social dependence.

context.title: Cost in life
context.text: Thoreau measures an expense partly by the labour and attention needed to pay for it. Cheapness and simplicity become philosophical questions.
context.takeaway: Money is not the only unit of account.

notice.why: The voice moves between naturalist and provocateur.
Solitude remains in conversation with social life.

opening: Thoreau builds a small house near a pond and begins keeping accounts. He wants to know how much life the ordinary necessities actually cost, and how many supposedly necessary expenses merely purchase more work. His experiment leaves time for beans, visitors, ice, birds, and thoughts that a busier arrangement might never permit. The book can be funny, exacting, and infuriatingly confident, but its provocation is concrete: examine what occupies your days closely enough to discover whether you would choose the bargain again.
